messages:
sam (AE): NimblePay requested a concise perf sweep: steady 130 qps chat (512 seq), short spikes to 700 qps, compare redwood-7b-4bit vs redwood-7b-fp32, and provide CI commands + redact proof. Can we scope and give ballpark cost?

tara (SRE): Plan: 15m warm, 30m steady @130 qps, bursts: 3m@300, 3m@500, 5m@700, cooldown 8m. Capture p50/p95/p99/p99.9, gpu slice util, batch distribution, cache hit rate. Tag runs customer=nimblepay bench=multi-sla.

jin (SE): Use seq_in 128, seq_out 384 => 512. Recommend run both warm and cold cache for 4bit to show variance. Add routing fallback to fp32 during >500ms p95 for >10s.

omar (Solutions Eng): Quick cost sketch: assume 70 tok/resp. For steady 130 qps that's ~9.1k tok/s. List-rate approx: fp32 $0.0000010/token, 4bit $0.00000036/token. I'll prepare a short spreadsheet with per-run totals and a committed discount example.

ci-bot: bench job nimblepay-sweep-v1 queued (id: ci-nimblepay-2025-11-03)

tara (SRE): CI command (pasteable):
```bash
./bench/run_bench.sh \
  --profile profiles/nimblepay_sweep.json \
  --model redwood-7b-4bit \
  --duration 3600 \
  --out gs://redwood-temp/nimblepay/run-4bit.json \
  --meta "customer=nimblepay,run=multi-sla" \
  --redact-prompts true
```
Redact flag hashes inputs; we store only hashes + token counts for compliance. Profile & seed uploaded to gs://redwood-temp/nimblepay/profiles/.

tara (SRE): interim: steady 30m on 4bit done. p95 150ms, p99 340ms, p99.9 700ms. gpu_util 61%, batch median 8, kv_hit 68%. Partial results uploaded.

omar (Solutions Eng): Interim looks good. 4bit meets steady p95 <200ms. fp32 run next to compare tails.

tara (SRE): final: runs complete. Topline: 4bit warm steady p95 155ms, burst@700 p95 510ms, burst@700 p99.9 1.05s. fp32 warm steady p95 98ms, burst@700 p95 245ms, burst@700 p99.9 680ms. Observed cost delta ~3.0x fp32 vs 4bit. Artifacts & redact manifest uploaded to gs://redwood-temp/nimblepay/final/.

jin (SE): Recommendation: If NimblePay needs tight burst tail SLAs pick fp32 on Dedicated or pre-warm caches aggressively. If cost is the priority, 4bit warm is a good compromise with fallback to fp32 during sustained tail degradation.

omar (Solutions Eng): I'll attach the cost appendix and three pricing scenarios to the deck.

sam (AE): Great. Action items: tara upload final logs + redact proof (owner), jin draft one-pager, omar finalize cost appendix, sam prep deck. Meeting Friday 10am PT. :thumbsup:
